llm.summary: The skill mostly matches its stated purpose (a CLI client for the Sparki video-editing API) but contains a few unexplained/incoherent items — most notably a required 'uv' binary and a Homebrew install step for it even though the shipped code is a Python CLI that does not use 'uv'.

dimensions.detail: The package is a Python CLI that uses httpx/typer/pydantic to call Sparki HTTP APIs and manage local config/history. However the registry metadata and SKILL.md require the 'uv' binary and the install spec installs a Homebrew formula named 'uv' — the source code contains no references to 'uv'. Requiring and auto-installing 'uv' is disproportionate and unexplained for a pure-Python Sparki client.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The runtime instructions are explicit and largely limited to: checking/setting an API key, telling users how to provide files (local path or Telegram Mini App), and running sparki CLI commands (setup, upload, edit, status, download). The skill writes config/history under ~/.openclaw and reads an optional SPARKI_UPLOAD_TG_LINK env var. There is no hidden exfiltration or obfuscated endpoints in the code; network calls go to a base URL (DEFAULT_BASE_URL = https://agent-api.sparki.io). One minor mismatch: the SKILL.md metadata declares only SPARKI_API_KEY, but code also reads SPARKI_UPLOAD_TG_LINK from env (not declared).
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Install metadata only installs a Homebrew formula 'uv' (creates binary 'uv'). The project itself is a Python package (pyproject.toml) with entrypoint 'sparki' and typical Python dependencies; there is no install step to install the Python package or its dependencies. The Homebrew 'uv' install appears unrelated to the code and is disproportionate; it's unclear whether the platform will also install the Python package or expects 'uv' for some external reason.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares a single required credential (SPARKI_API_KEY) which is appropriate for an API client. The code will also optionally read SPARKI_UPLOAD_TG_LINK (not listed in requires.env) and saves the API key into ~/.openclaw/config/sparki.json in plaintext. No other unrelated credentials are requested. Requiring only SPARKI_API_KEY is proportionate, but the plaintext local storage of the key and the undeclared SPARKI_UPLOAD_TG_LINK env var are worth noting.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always:false and default autonomous invocation settings are standard. The skill stores its own config and history under ~/.openclaw (per-skill user files) and does not modify other skills or system-wide settings. This level of persistence is expected for a CLI-style skill.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance:
This skill appears to be a legitimate CLI client for the Sparki video-editing API, but there are a few things to check before installing or providing credentials:

- Ask the publisher why the 'uv' binary is required. The provided Python code does not reference 'uv', yet the metadata and install step force a Homebrew install of 'uv'. That is unusual and should be explained or removed.
- Confirm how the platform will install the Python package and its dependencies (pyproject.toml lists typer/httpx/pydantic). The registry's install step only installs 'uv' — make sure the Python CLI will actually be available to run.
- The skill saves your API key in plaintext at ~/.openclaw/config/sparki.json. If you proceed, create a sparki-specific API key with minimal scope and rotate/delete it when no longer needed.
- Verify the API endpoints and domain (DEFAULT_BASE_URL = https://agent-api.sparki.io and homepage https://sparki.io). If you don’t recognize or trust those hosts, do not supply credentials.
- The skill will request local file paths (it uploads local files). Do not provide sensitive or private videos unless you trust the service and have reviewed privacy/terms.

If the author can justify or remove the 'uv' requirement and clarify how the Python CLI will be installed, the package would look coherent. Without that explanation the extra binary/install step is an unexplained risk.
